root_cause.text: The driver registers the IRQ handler using devm_request_irq() before registering the power supply with devm_power_supply_register(), causing the power supply to be freed (due to reverse devm cleanup order) before the IRQ is unregistered, leading to a use-after-free when an interrupt fires after the power supply is freed but before the IRQ handler is removed.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "Using the `devm_` variant for requesting IRQ _before_ the `devm_` variant for allocating/registering the `power_supply` handle, means that the `power_supply` handle will be deallocated/unregistered _before_ the interrupt handler (since `devm_` naturally deallocates in reverse allocation order). This means that during removal, there is a race condition where an interrupt can fire just _after_ the `power_supply` handle has been freed, *but* just _before_ the corresponding unregistration of the IRQ handler has run." The patch moves the `devm_request_irq()` call after the power supply registration.

Author: Wenyou Yang <wenyou.yang@atmel.com>

    power: supply: act8945a_charger: Add status change update support
    
    Add the charger status change interrupt support, it will report
    the power supply changed event.
    
    This interrupt is generated by one of the conditions as below:
     - the state machine jumps out of or into the EOC state
     - the CHGIN input voltage goes out of or into the va
bic_trace_step.reason: The probe function registers the IRQ handler (devm_request_irq) before the power supply (devm_power_supply_register), which is the problematic order. However, the code includes a protection mechanism: an init_done flag that is set to true only after all initialization in probe, and the interrupt handler (act8945a_status_changed) checks this flag before accessing charger->psy. In the remove function (act8945a_charger_remove), init_done is set to false and the work is canceled with cancel_work_sync, ensuring that after removal starts, the interrupt handler will not access the freed power supply. Therefore, the use-after-free vulnerability is prevented, and the code already contains the fix.
